fair_value.method: Blend of forward EV/EBITDA (~$36), forward P/E (~$38) and a conservative long-term-copper DCF/NAV (~$30) for Ero Copper; assumes 2027 copper ~$5.75/lb (below the ~$6.5-6.8/lb September 2026 record), ~78kt Cu, ~106M diluted shares, net debt falling from $453M to ~$150M by end-2027.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E EBITDA ~$650M (revenue ~$1.35B: ~78kt Cu at $5.75/lb plus ~80koz Au at ~$3,800/oz; ~48% margin) x 6.0x = EV $3.9B, less ~$150M end-2027 net debt = $3.75B / 106M shares ~ $35-36. Peer/historical range 5-7x; current forward multiple ~5.7x per Seeking Alpha.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Market in Sep-2027 prices 2028E EPS (Caraiba Pilar shaft full benefit, ~+1/3 Cu output): 2028E EPS ~$4.75 at $5.50/lb Cu x 8x = $38. Cross-check: 2026 consensus EPS $4.22 x 9x = $38.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Normalized post-2027 FCF ~$350M/yr (EBITDA $650M - sustaining capex $200M - tax $80M - interest $20M) at long-term Cu ~$5.00-5.25/lb, 15-year life, 10% real-ish discount rate -> ~$2.66B; plus Furnas 60% option ~$0.5B; less ~$0.35B net debt -> ~$2.8B / 106M = ~$26.5 today, rolled forward one year ~$29-30.

bear.story: Copper retraces from record highs to ~$4.50/lb as tariff-driven US/LME split unwinds and Escondida risk fades; Caraiba Pilar shaft completion slips past end-2026 pushing 2028 growth out a year; BRL strengthens after election, lifting costs; Tucumã/Xavantina keep underdelivering (Ero has a history of guidance cuts). Stock rerates to ~4.5x depressed EBITDA.

base.story: Copper stays elevated but off peak ($5.50-6.00/lb); 2026 guidance (67.5-77.5kt) met, capex falls sharply in 2027, revolver repaid and a shareholder-return program announced; shaft bottomed around year-end with 2028 uplift on track. Multiple stays ~6x forward EBITDA; stock roughly flat-to-up modestly.

bull.story: Copper supply deficit persists (Chile output weakest in 19 years), prices hold $6.50+/lb; Tucumã reaches nameplate with modular filters, shaft delivered on time, Furnas PFS in 2027 shows a sizable high-grade project; FCF inflection plus buybacks/dividend drive rerating to 7x+ and EPS $6+.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$21 (-45%) the stock would be pricing either a copper collapse toward $4/lb or a material operational failure (shaft delay/failure at Caraiba, Tucumã plant not sustaining ~250kt/month, balance sheet re-leveraging); at 2027 production and even $4.75 copper the business supports ~$25+, so trading there likely means the growth/deleveraging thesis is broken rather than ordinary 60%-vol noise.

catalysts.event: Escondida strike vote (28-30 Sep) - copper supply risk
Brazil presidential election first round (runoff 2026-10-25) - BRL/cost and country-risk impact
Q3 2026 financial results; revolver repayment progress
Caraiba Pilar external shaft targeted to reach bottom by year-end; Furnas Phase 3 drilling completion; Tucumã modular filters commissioned Q4
2026 production vs guidance and 2027 guidance / capex step-down
Q4 2026 results; possible first shareholder-return program once revolver repaid
Furnas pre-feasibility study; updated Tucumã reserves

key_uncertainties: Copper price path from record ~$6.8/lb (Comex, 22 Sep 2026); tariff-driven US premium could unwind
Timing of Caraiba Pilar shaft completion and the 2028 production uplift
Sustained Tucumã throughput/recoveries and Xavantina gold underperformance (gold guided to low end, costs raised)
BRL direction around the October 2026 election (FX hedges ~$40-45M/yr gain; unhedged strength ~+$0.10/lb Cu costs)
Ero's track record of downward guidance revisions
Gold by-product price and Furnas earn-in capital needs
reasoning: Ero Copper (NYSE/TSX: ERO) has doubled in a year on a record copper price and a successful deleveraging (net debt $453M, 0.8x vs 2.6x peak; Q2-26 adj. EBITDA $144M, adj. EPS $0.83, OCF $138M) plus Tucumã ramp-up. 2026 Cu guidance 67.5-77.5kt reaffirmed at C1 $2.15-2.35/lb; capex $285-330M is the peak, with a 'significant decline' in 2027 and the Caraiba shaft giving full benefit in 2028 (~+1/3 Cu). At $37.87 the stock (~$4.0B mkt cap, ~$4.4B EV) sits at ~9x 2026 consensus EPS $4.22 and ~5.7-6.8x forward EBITDA - fair-to-cheap at spot copper but largely pricing copper near records. My valuation normalizes copper to ~$5.50-5.75/lb for 2027-28 and gets ~$35 blended (EV/EBITDA $36, P/E $38, conservative DCF $30); sell-side mean target ~$40.7 (range $35-44, 8 buy/10 hold) and a $50 Buy (Seeking Alpha) bracket this. Scenarios: bear $22 (25%), base $38 (50%), bull $55 (25%) -> mean ~$38, median ~$36-37. For the ladder I used a lognormal centered at a ~$36.5 median (slightly below spot, reflecting mean-reversion risk in copper offset by FCF inflection/buybacks) with sigma ~0.50 - below the 64% trailing realized vol because the trailing year included a violent rerating/deleveraging, but well above a large-cap's 25-35% given single-commodity, single-country (Brazil election Oct 4) and single-shaft execution risk. Slightly fattened the far-left tail for a copper crash. Research limited to web sources; no consensus 2027 figures accessible (paywalled); CMD (Sep 14) detail was paywalled so no confirmed multi-year guidance beyond statements quoted.
